payload.claim: `revert_exempt` is built from `entry["failures"]` of `killed` probe entries, which are `Failure.code` values from the repo's own `tests` gate. `saffron/gates/core/revert.py:310-314` documents, as a measured fact, that this repo's `tests` gate keys `failures[].code` on the caught exception type on its common path, and only reaches a real node id through a fallback. `probe_findings`/`check_probe` always invoke the tests gate with an empty subset (`saffron/cell/session.py:1843` and `saffron/probe.py:213`, `run_tests([])`), which never exercises that fallback in `.saffron/gates/tests.py` (the fallback only fires when a non-empty handed `subset` fails to collect). So for assertion failures reported on the common path, `check_probe`'s `killing = tuple(n.failure.code for n in new if n.failure.code in counted)` compares an exception-type string against a set of real test node ids and can never match, meaning `probe_verdict` can never actually read `killed` for this repo in production. `killed` therefore stays empty, `revert_exempt` is always `[]`, and the whole b-4a63b7 exemption mechanism is inert for Saffron's own gate even though the new tests (which fake `code=name`) make `criteria`/`witness` report green, so acceptance criterion 2's claim that such a task reaches `READY_FOR_REVIEW` is not actually met against this repo's real `tests` gate.
